title: validate_attachments: filename contains('..') rejects valid filenames
description:
What is awkward: the check 'a.filename.contains("..")' rejects valid filenames like "file..txt" or "v2..3.tar.gz" because they contain the two-character sequence "..". The intent is to block path traversal.

Suggested rewrite: check for path traversal sequences specifically — a.filename.contains("../") || a.filename.contains("..\\") || a.filename == ".." — rather than rejecting any filename containing two adjacent dots. This is more precise and won't surprise users whose files have double-dot names.
